platform.windows: compiles; the Windows session path is T6 and no Windows peer run has been recorded

upstream.role: the peer is a Mihomo `listeners:` endpoint; the Rust kernel is the client and a controlled loopback sink records what arrived

socks5.notes: the peer replies success after its own SOCKS5 handshake but before dialing, so the positive case is judged by the tagged bytes the sink received

http.notes: Mihomo's HTTP inbound writes 200 before dialing, so only the receiving side proves a positive tunnel; a wrong credential is answered with 407 and the kernel reports 502

ss.notes: AEAD 2017 framing and both directions (the client reads the server's salt); loopback peers cover aes-128-gcm and chacha20-ietf-poly1305

trojan.peer: listeners: type: trojan with a self-signed certificate
trojan.notes: wrong password and an untrusted certificate are both checked; the peer closes silently on the first, the client refuses the second

vless.notes: the ws case records that the client must not send Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: Mihomo reads a non-empty value as Xray 0-RTT early data

anytls.notes: one stream per connection, protocol version 2; the server's SYNACK is not awaited before the payload is sent, as sing's client does

dialer-proxy.peer: two Mihomo listeners (mixed as the exit hop, socks as the first hop)
dialer-proxy.notes: only a socks5 hop can carry another hop; a closed first hop fails the dial instead of falling back to DIRECT, and other chains are rejected at load time or with a chain error

notCovered: UDP: the mixed inbound has no UDP ASSOCIATE, so no protocol family carries UDP traffic end to end (the SS datagram codec is unit-tested)
separate `listeners:` entries on the Rust side (T5); the peer side uses them because the peer is Mihomo
platforms other than macOS arm64; DNS answers, rule families beyond T2's list, TUN/system-proxy takeover (T6)
runMode: serially (--test-threads=1); the cases are ignored by default so the default cargo test neither fails nor implies interop
